question: Should OpenClaw officially own and publish the LLMRouter provider, or require LLMRouter to maintain it as an external ClawHub plugin?
rationale: The existing plugin API can support the integration either way, but official package ownership endorses a commercial provider and creates continuing release, security, and documentation obligations that code review cannot choose.

options.title: Provider-owned ClawHub plugin
options.body: Require LLMRouter to maintain and publish the corrected provider plugin externally, leaving OpenClaw core limited to its existing provider SDK and generic custom-provider path.

options.title: Sponsor official provider
options.body: Accept official `@openclaw` ownership after live catalog resolution, production behavior proof, dependency authorization, and an identified long-term owner are complete.

recommendation.title: Provider-owned ClawHub plugin
recommendation.body: Require LLMRouter to maintain and publish the corrected provider plugin externally, leaving OpenClaw core limited to its existing provider SDK and generic custom-provider path.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest recently merged official-provider precedent and is the documented project decision lead.
